sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Manheim Township?
sections.html:
Manheim Township is a Lancaster County municipality of 43,977 people where the biggest issue for sellers is the countywide reassessment that takes effect for the 2027 tax year. A certificate of use and occupancy and a 2 percent transfer tax round out the local rules.

This page covers Manheim Township, which sits directly north of Lancaster city. Lancaster County also has a separate borough named Manheim, so check the municipality on your tax bill before relying on any local rule. The township has no ZIP code of its own, so owners carry a Lititz, Lancaster or Leola mailing address depending on where the house sits.

Sellers here choose among a retail listing, a sale by owner and a direct purchase for cash. The sections below explain the paperwork that applies to all three.

sections.h2: Where is Manheim Township and how big is it?
sections.html:
The township covers about 24 square miles and ranks as the second largest municipality in Lancaster County, behind the city itself. It was established in 1729, and its southern boundary meets the Lancaster city limits.

The township's communities include Neffsville, Dillerville and Landis Valley. Population counts show how steadily it has grown:

  • 9,289 residents in 1950.
  • 21,539 in 1970.
  • 33,697 in 2000.
  • 43,977 in 2020.

The 2000 census put the median age at 43, with 21 percent of residents 65 or older.

sections.h2: How does the Manheim Township School District affect a sale?
sections.html:
The school district is coterminous with the township, so a home inside the township boundary is in the district and a home outside it is not. That clean match makes the address check simple for a buyer.

The district runs Manheim Township High School, a virtual high school, Manheim Township Middle School, Landis Run Intermediate School and six elementary schools: Brecht, Bucher, Neff, Nitrauer, Reidenbaugh and Schaeffer. Buyers with children usually ask which elementary school serves a street, and the district office can confirm that from an address.

The township itself does not bill or collect property taxes. Lancaster County assesses the property, while the elected tax collector and the school district collect the bills.

sections.h2: What is the 2027 Lancaster County reassessment?
sections.html:
Lancaster County reassessed every parcel at current market value, and the new values apply to the 2027 tax year. The previous assessments were based on 2018 values, and the county says the new notices should land near what a property would sell for today. Notices were mailed on June 15, 2026.

The county used valid arm's-length residential sales from 2022 through 2024, adjusted for acreage, square footage, porches, garages and bathrooms. State law requires each taxing body to adjust its millage so it does not collect more revenue only because values moved, but the tax on an individual house can still rise or fall. County and municipal millage for 2027 is set near the end of December 2026, and school millage for the 2027-2028 year is set in June 2027. The reassessment does not change 2026-27 school taxes.

The reassessment appeal deadline was August 3, 2026, the first business day after August 1, and it has passed. The county says the next opportunity for an annual appeal is 2028. Ask the Property Assessment Office at 717-299-8381 what applies to a house that sold or changed after the notices went out.

sections.h2: Does Manheim Township require an inspection to sell?
sections.html:
No. The township states that it does not require an inspection before settlement. A certificate of use and occupancy can still be requested by the parties to the deal, and the zoning ordinance has required one for every structure since 1944.

If you need a copy, contact the Code Compliance Department with the property address, the home type (single-family, townhouse or duplex) and whether any part of the basement is finished. Staff check the records and send a copy if one is on file. If none exists, the owner or an agent applies in person at the township office, pays a $50 residential filing fee and books an inspection with a code official.

sections.h2: How much is the transfer tax in Manheim Township?
sections.html:
The township Treasurer's Office FAQ puts the realty transfer tax at 2 percent of the value transferred. The Commonwealth receives 1 percent, and the township and school district share the other 1 percent.

The Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds collects the tax when the deed is recorded. The state notes that both buyer and seller are liable for it, and the sale contract decides how it is split. Certain family transfers and property passed by inheritance are exempt from the state portion, so ask the recorder before assuming a deed is taxable.

Real estate tax bills combine the county and township taxes and go out by March 1. If a lender pays your taxes from escrow, send the lender a copy of the bill.

sections.h2: What rules apply if I am selling a rental in Manheim Township?
sections.html:
Manheim Township has licensed rental properties since 2022, and an annual license costs $50 per building. Each rental unit is inspected at least once every five years, and one- and two-unit buildings have every unit inspected.

  • Owners living more than 25 miles from the township must name a responsible local agent.
  • Inspection fees run from $40 for one unit to $250 for buildings with 51 or more units.
  • The code compliance office handles applications, renewals and de-registration.

A landlord who sells should ask the code office how to de-register or transfer the license, and should hand the buyer the latest inspection results.

sections.h2: Should I list the house or take a cash offer?
sections.html:
Both work in Manheim Township, and the better choice depends on the condition of the house and how soon you need to close. A listing exposes the house to more buyers but adds showings and inspection negotiations. A cash purchase can be scheduled around your move.

  • Request your certificate of use and occupancy early so a missing certificate does not delay the closing.
  • Look up your 2027 reassessed value on the county property search site and compare it with the price you are weighing.
  • Subtract the 2 percent transfer tax share you agree to, plus any mortgage payoff, to estimate net proceeds.

If a buyer asks for repairs, compare the cost against a quote for selling as-is.

faqs.q: Is Manheim Township the same as the borough of Manheim?
faqs.a: No. Manheim Township is a separate municipality that borders Lancaster city and has its own school district and township government. Lancaster County also has a borough named Manheim.

faqs.q: Does Manheim Township require a certificate of use and occupancy when I sell?
faqs.a: Not as a condition of settlement. The township does not inspect before closing, but buyers or lenders may ask for a copy. If none is on file, the residential filing fee is $50 and an inspection is scheduled.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a Manheim Township sale?
faqs.a: It is 2 percent of the value transferred. The state gets 1 percent, and the township and school district share the other 1 percent. The Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds collects it.

faqs.q: When did the Lancaster County reassessment take effect?
faqs.a: The new values apply to the 2027 tax year. Notices were mailed June 15, 2026, and the appeal deadline of August 3, 2026 has passed. The next annual appeal opportunity is 2028.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Manheim Township?
faqs.a: The elected tax collector and the school district collect the bills. Lancaster County sets the assessment, and the township does not bill or collect property taxes itself.
